title: Highest-Protein Cheeses: Ranking per 100 Grams and Serving

seo.title: Highest-Protein Cheeses: Ranking
seo.meta_description: Compare Parmesan, Romano, Gruyère, Swiss, cheddar and mozzarella by protein per 100 grams and realistic serving size.
seo.search_intent: Compare cheeses by protein and understand the effect of moisture and aging.

excerpt: Parmesan dominates per 100 grams because it is so concentrated, but most people do not eat it in the same portion as a fresh cheese. Once serving size enters the picture, the ranking tells a different story.
content_html:
Water explains much of the cheese protein ranking. The more a cheese is pressed, aged and dried, the more protein appears in every 100 grams. The same process also concentrates fat, calcium and sodium.

That is why Parmesan can win easily by weight while a much larger bowl of cottage cheese can deliver more total protein in an actual meal.

Protein per 100 grams: aged cheeses lead

CheeseApprox. protein
Parmesan35.8 g
Pecorino Romano~31.9 g
Gruyère~29.8 g
Swiss/Emmental style~27 g
Provolone~25.6 g
Cheddar~25 g
Gouda~25 g
Low-moisture mozzarella~24 g
Feta~14 g
Cottage cheese~11–13 g

Parmesan: enormous by weight, more ordinary by serving

Parmesan provides about 35.8 g protein/100 g, one of the highest values in the category. But a normal serving is closer to 1 ounce / 28 g, which supplies about 10 g protein along with roughly 110 calories and substantial sodium.

The 100-gram number describes concentration; it does not describe how people usually eat the cheese.

Romano and Gruyère follow the same pattern

Romano is around 32 g/100 g and Gruyère near 30 g. A 1-ounce serving provides roughly 8–9 g protein. Both are relatively dry cheeses, which is exactly why their milk solids are so concentrated.

Cheddar, Gouda and Provolone cluster together

These sit around 25–26 g/100 g. One ounce provides about 7 g protein, close to the 6–7 g in a large egg.

At this point, fractions of a gram matter less than taste, sodium, fat and how much you actually use.

“Mozzarella” can mean two different moisture levels

Low-moisture mozzarella can reach about 24 g/100 g, while fresh mozzarella contains much more water and may be closer to 18–20 g.

The protein itself has not fundamentally changed; the concentration has, because one product contains much more water.

Fresh cheeses lose the 100-gram race and can win the bowl

Cottage cheese is often around 11–13 g/100 g, about one-third of Parmesan by weight. But a 1-cup / ~200 g bowl can provide 22–26 g protein — more total protein than a normal Parmesan serving.

Fresh cheeses also tend to have lower calorie density because they carry more water, especially in lower-fat versions.

Aging concentrates; it does not create protein

As water leaves the cheese, more milk solids remain in every 100 grams. Protein, calcium, fat and often sodium all become more concentrated. The aging process is changing proportions, not manufacturing new protein.

What normal servings contribute

CheeseServingProtein
Parmesan1 oz / 28 g10 g
Gruyère1 oz / 28 g8–9 g
Cheddar1 oz / 28 g7 g
Low-moisture mozzarella2 oz / 56 g13 g
Cottage cheese1 cup / ~200 g22–26 g

The “best” cheese depends on the job

A small amount of grated Parmesan brings intense flavor and meaningful protein; a bowl of cottage cheese can function as the main protein component of a snack or meal. Those are different uses, and serving size captures that difference better than a single per-100-gram ranking.

Hard cheeses can be excellent calcium sources but also concentrate saturated fat and sodium. A lower-fat cottage cheese may have less protein by weight and far fewer calories per 100 g.

The takeaway

Parmesan, Romano and Gruyère lead by concentration. Once real serving sizes enter the picture, moisture and portion size can completely change which cheese contributes the most protein. The ranking is useful; the serving explains it.

faq.question: Which cheese has the most protein?
faq.answer: Parmesan is among the most concentrated at about 35.8 g/100 g, followed by Romano near 32 g and Gruyère near 30 g.

faq.question: Why does aged cheese have more protein?
faq.answer: It contains less water, so protein and other milk solids are more concentrated by weight.

faq.question: Is cottage cheese low in protein?
faq.answer: It is less concentrated, around 11–13 g/100 g, but a full cup can provide more than 20 g protein.
